disposition_mapping.rationale: The step conflated mechanical cadence/timetable governance with judgment-laden assumptions-pack curation. Council converged (finance_domain's proposal, adopted by hitl_designer and emerging_economy) on splitting these: cadence and template distribution become an orchestration-supported governance act (TS-01), while the assumptions-pack content (which corporate targets apply, which events are material) merges downstream with driver refresh (TS-03) since both answer 'what changed since last cycle' and should reach BUs as one coherent package rather than two releases that can drift out of sync.

Extraction and mapping mechanics are automated, but the council majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, accounting_standards, agentic_architect) insists the cutoff/completeness discipline (KB-03) survive as more than an embedded code gate: a dual ingestion track (automated plus first-class manual path for non-integrated entities, per emerging_economy) feeds identical validation logic, and a named human certification sign-off attaches to the baseline each cycle, with failures escalated rather than silently passed through. This satisfies FPA-R-02's requirement that consolidation consume a validated closed-period actuals baseline.

Mechanical FX and run-rate drivers auto-refresh with source, date and exchange-difference explicitly tagged (KB-08, conceded by maximalist and specified further by hitl_designer/agentic_architect); judgment-based drivers (pricing, headcount, volume) retain a named owner and contemporaneously logged rationale (hitl_designer's structural requirement, adopted across the council), curated by the FP&A analyst. The council majority rejected maximalist's proposal to fold this judgment into the BU submission step: a distinct, dated FP&A-owned artefact is needed so a bad outcome can be diagnosed as bad instruction versus bad BU execution.

Five of seven council members (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) independently rejected the agent-drafts/BU-overrides model on anchoring-bias and accountability grounds: a BU lead reviewing a plausible AI draft under deadline pressure scrutinises it less than a blank template forces, and the commentary that constitutes this step's actual value depends on the preparer having generated the number, not approved someone else's. BU finance leads remain the accountable originators; automation is limited to embedded template validation providing immediate feedback, and templates are made offline-capable per emerging_economy's non-negotiable.

Roll-up, intercompany matching and coherence checks are automated as a continuous rule engine with a hard dependency on the validated actuals baseline (satisfying FPA-R-02 and KB-03 by construction), but 'chase and correct anomalous submissions' remains named human judgment with a defined SLA, per the near-unanimous council view that anomaly resolution requires business context a system lacks (KB-05). Per accounting_standards' KB-06 concern, raised independently and unanswered by the automation-forward positions, any change to the consolidation/computation methodology itself is now surfaced as a distinct disclosed basis-change event, separate from anomaly flagging, so a redefinition of the rules is never quietly absorbed. The intercompany check is retained as a load-bearing internal control though the council (accounting_standards) notes KB-14 does not itself reach internal forecasting.

FPA-R-01 requires this function survive, and the council decisively rejected maximalist's single-actor merge of consolidation and variance analysis: pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect and accounting_standards independently converged on the same failure mode from different angles (data-quality-narrated-as-business-movement, single-point-of-failure concentration, loss of a KB-06 basis-change seam, loss of tool-boundary observability). The synthesis holds that FPA-R-01's requirement is judged on functional separation, not mere step-nameability: bridge arithmetic is automated, but this remains its own step with human-authored narrative and risk judgment, distinct from TS-05.

FPA-R-03 requires survival; the council (hitl_designer's central concern, adopted by pragmatist, maximalist and finance_domain) held that merely preserving the step's name and position risks a rubber stamp once upstream mechanics are automated. The redesign feeds this step an exception-curated briefing — material movements, judgment-driver rationale, resolved anomalies, basis-change disclosures — rather than a full re-derivation, and requires the approval record be traceable to the specific items reviewed, making the challenge session substantive rather than ceremonial.

FPA-R-05 requires survival and FPA-R-04 requires strict ordering after approval. The council converged (agentic_architect's design, adopted by hitl_designer and pragmatist) on making the ordering an architectural invariant: publication is event-gated strictly on the TS-07 approval signal, never time- or best-effort-gated. Per accounting_standards' KB-02 anchor, the archive preserves both the numeric version and its linked assumptions-basis (not just a version snapshot), and per agentic_architect's reversibility requirement the record is written before distribution to allow unambiguous rollback. Distribution retains a non-cloud-dependent channel per emerging_economy's non-negotiable.

steps.description: Confirm the forecast horizon, granularity and cadence for the cycle as a named governance act by the FP&A manager; trigger cycle initiation via orchestration tooling on the rolling calendar; issue timetable and templates to business units through a multi-channel, offline-capable distribution path (not cloud-portal-only), so entities without standing connectivity are not excluded. This step carries only the mechanical/calendar content of the former initiation step; assumption curation is relocated to TS-03 so that judgment content is not bundled with pure cadence mechanics.
steps.name: Cycle governance and timetable issuance

steps.description: Ingest closed-period actuals via an automated GL/management-reporting feed for integrated entities and via a manual template-upload-and-reconciliation path for entities without system integration, applying identical completeness and consistency validation logic to both tracks so neither is treated as a degraded exception. Enforce a hard period-lock gate: actuals for a period not yet closed cannot load as baseline. Preserve revenue-recognition timing embedded in actuals when remapping into forecast structure. A named FP&A analyst issues a dated certification sign-off each cycle confirming the gate fired correctly; any completeness or reconciliation break routes to the analyst as an explicit exception with a resolution path, never silently forwarded as validated.
steps.name: Actuals ingestion and validation (dual-track)
outputs: closed-period actuals (validated baseline) loaded to forecast model

steps.description: Assemble the refreshed assumptions pack (macro indicators, corporate targets, known business events) together with driver assumption refresh, since both answer 'what changed since last cycle' and must travel as one coherent package to business units. FX rates and actual run-rates are refreshed mechanically, with rate source, rate date and the resulting exchange-difference delta logged and retained as a separately traceable component, never netted into a blended figure. Volume, pricing, headcount and cost-inflation assumptions remain judgment calls: each is set by a named business-input owner with a contemporaneously logged rationale, curated by the FP&A analyst as accountable owner of the assembled driver set. This artefact stays distinct from, and upstream of, BU submission (TS-04) so that a poor forecast outcome can be diagnosed as bad instruction versus bad BU execution. Note: automating the mechanical FX/run-rate computation displaces manual re-keying work; the target state requires this displaced time be redirected to exception review and judgment-driver curation rather than assumed away, though the council notes this commitment is not independently schema-enforceable and rests on rationale, not a checkable field.
steps.name: Assumptions and driver refresh with named judgment ownership
outputs: Updated driver assumptions with named owner and logged rationale

steps.description: BU finance leads originate forecast submissions (revenue, cost, headcount, capex) against the refreshed drivers, using offline-capable templates with embedded validation (schema completeness, headcount-to-cost coherence, continuity checks) that gives immediate feedback at the point of entry rather than a later chase cycle. The BU finance lead remains the accountable preparer of the number, not a reviewer of a machine-generated draft: commentary explaining changes since the prior forecast is human-authored and attributed to a named preparer, preserving the evidentiary basis subsequent steps rely on.
steps.name: Business unit forecast submission
outputs: BU forecast submissions with human-authored, attributed commentary

steps.description: An automated rule engine performs roll-up, intercompany matching and headcount-to-cost coherence checks continuously as submissions arrive, and refuses to consolidate if the closed-period actuals baseline is missing or stale, enforcing direct, hard consumption of that baseline. Any change to the consolidation or computation methodology itself (a new formula, a redefined coherence ratio) is surfaced as a disclosed basis-change event, logged distinctly from anomaly flagging on submitted data. Anomalous submissions above threshold are escalated to a named FP&A analyst with a defined resolution SLA; investigating, chasing and correcting anomalous submissions remains human judgment and is never auto-resolved. This step remains a distinct checkpoint from variance analysis (TS-06) so that a data-quality break cannot be absorbed into the same motion that later explains it as a business movement.
inputs: BU forecast submissions with human-authored, attributed commentary
steps.name: Consolidation, validation and exception resolution

steps.description: Automated bridge computation quantifies movements by driver and business unit against budget and the prior forecast, immediately upon TS-05's validated output. FX-isolated components are shown separately using TS-03's exchange-difference tag; basis-change events flagged in TS-05 are displayed as a distinct bridge component, not absorbed into business-performance variance. The FP&A analyst supplies human-authored narrative and risk/opportunity judgment on materiality-flagged items; arithmetic is delegable, the forward-looking explanation of what is real risk versus noise is not. Kept as its own step, separate from consolidation, to preserve a seam at which a data-integrity break can be caught before it is narrated as a business story.
steps.name: Variance and bridge analysis

steps.description: Management reviews an exception-curated briefing pack — material movements, judgment-driver rationale flags, resolved anomalies, and basis-change disclosures — rather than a full re-derivation of every mechanical number, so that automating the upstream mechanics makes this review more substantive, not less. Challenge sessions address the flagged items directly; directed revisions are incorporated. Approval is recorded as a discrete, named, dated act, and the approval record is traceable to the specific items actually reviewed, not merely a sign-off timestamp.
steps.name: Exception-based management review and approval

steps.description: Publication fires only on receipt of the TS-07 approval event — a hard, structural gate, not a time- or best-effort trigger, so it is architecturally impossible for a forecast to be released without recorded sign-off. Planning systems and reporting baselines are updated and the forecast pack distributed through a channel that does not require continuous cloud connectivity or per-seat licensing (e.g., file-based/email pack alongside any BI publication), reaching stakeholders regardless of local infrastructure. Before distribution, an immutable version record is written preserving both the numeric version and its linked assumptions-basis (assumptions pack, FX rate vintage, computation basis), so a post-publish error can be rolled back to a prior published baseline without ambiguity.
steps.name: Automated publication and archival, approval-gated
